answer: Admission-Window Interleave Enforcement. New identities must complete a fixed sequence of opal-tagged heartbeat exchanges spread across at least one full network horizon before their messages are routed. The relay admits one probe per quartz interval, so each identity occupies a distinct timing slot and duplicates collapse onto the same window. An attacker running N identities pays N times the wall-clock latency and N concurrent timer slots, making mass registration slow and observable.
